title: Elmwood Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
next_steps: Sofia to send onboarding guide, SSO/SAML docs, and SOW by 2027-11-03
Rita to schedule VPC/private deployment deep dive and runbook review by 2027-11-05
Daniel to share network contact and current firewall/IP allowlist by 2027-11-04
Marcus to set up weekly 30-min check-ins through the pilot period
action_items: Sofia Patel: Send onboarding guide, security brief, and SOW - due 2027-11-03
Rita Gomez: Schedule VPC deep dive and share deployment checklist - due 2027-11-05

summary: Kickoff for Elmwood Health onboarding to Redwood. Reviewed timelines, success criteria, roles, and high-level architecture choices (hosted vs private/VPC). Discussed security/compliance needs (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), initial integration tasks, and a plan for a short pilot. Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: Introductions; Success criteria & timeline; Networking & VPC needs; Security and compliance; Integration plan (API keys, test data); Pilot scope and metrics; Next steps and action items
transcript:
00:00 Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, nice to meet Elmwood team.
00:06 Daniel Park: Hi Sofia, Daniel here, CTO, we got Maya, Alex and Priya on the line as well. Thanks for setting this up.
00:13 Marcus Liu: Morning all, Marcus from Customer Success, I'll be leading the onboarding.
00:18 Rita Gomez: Rita, Solutions Eng, i'll handle the VPC and infra bits. Apologies for audio, i'm on a train so might be a little spotty.
00:25 Maya Thompson: Hey, thanks everyone. We're excited to get Redwood live for our triage and clinical summarization workflows.
00:33 Sofia Patel: Great, quick agenda — intros, what success looks like and timeline, security/compliance, infra options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), pilot scope, and next steps. Sound good?
00:42 Daniel Park: Yep. Our main goals: reduce triage time, better note summarization, and low latency for clinician-facing flows. We care about PHI handling, so need clarity on data residency and encryption.
00:56 Sofia Patel: Totally. On success criteria, would you say latency under 300ms for short-queries, and 95% accuracy on summary tests is the bar?
01:05 Maya Thompson: That aligns, though 300ms is ambitious — we can start with a 500ms target during pilot.
01:12 Rita Gomez: That's fine — we can instrument and measure. Quick question about deployment — do you anticipate private/VPC or hosted for pilot?
01:20 Daniel Park: For pilot we prefer hosted to move fast, but with private deployment roadmapped in quarter after pilot. We need to evaluate cost & network constraints.
01:29 Alex Rivera: From Ops side, we need to know what IPs to allow, and whether outbound connections are required. Also, do you support SAML SSO for audit access?
01:38 Sofia Patel: Yes, we support SAML/SSO and RBAC. We'll send the SSO setup doc. For hosted we require outbound to our control plane, yes; for private we can do VPC peering or air-gapped options.
01:50 Marcus Liu: On data handling — Redwood has options: hosted with short retention, or private for zero egress. We'll include our security brief.
01:58 Daniel Park: We need SOC 2 and encryption details, plus KMS integration for keys.
02:04 Rita Gomez: We do have KMS integrations for private deployments. For hosted, we can leverage customer-managed keys via our KMS passthrough depending on contract. I'll put the details in the security packet.
02:15 Priya Singh: Can you talk about model versioning and rollback? We need deterministic behavior for clinical audits.
02:22 Rita Gomez: Absolutely — Redwood supports pinning model versions and automatic rollbacks on regression triggers. There's also eval hooks so you can run your test suite on each deploy.
02:31 Maya Thompson: Good. On API integration, how complex is the SDK? We prefer Python internal services.
02:36 Sofia Patel: We have a Python SDK and REST endpoints. We'll share quickstart and sample code. API keys for pilot — we'll provision sandbox keys.
02:44 Alex Rivera: Any rate limits for sandbox? We plan for burst testing.
02:48 Sofia Patel: Sandbox has soft limits; for pilot we'll coordinate temporary quota increases.
02:52 Daniel Park: Perf testing — Rita, can we run a small benchmark to compare hosted latency vs a dedicated pool?
02:58 Rita Gomez: Yes, we can run a benchmark, we'll need sample traffic and sequences. Ideally a 1k-request run to capture p95/p99.
03:06 Marcus Liu: For pilot scope, propose: week 1 integration + test, week 2 pilot traffic with sample EHR data (de-identified), week 3 evaluate metrics and adjust. Aim for a 4-week pilot.
03:18 Maya Thompson: That timeline works. Week 1 we'll provide an anonymized dataset and expected prompts.
03:24 Daniel Park: One question on compliance documents — do you have an exec summary for legal? They like short answers.
03:29 Sofia Patel: Yes, we'll attach a one-page security exec summary along with SOC 2 and our standard DPA.
03:34 Priya Singh: On the network piece, Alex will need the allowlist. When can we expect that?
03:38 Rita Gomez: I'll follow up after this call with the URL list and ports. For hosted it's just outbound to a set of IPs, for private we'll share the VPC peering steps.
03:47 Alex Rivera: Great. Also curious about KV cache and performance — can you maintain session state for repeated clinician prompts?
03:52 Rita Gomez: Yes, we support KV cache and prefix caching to keep repeated context efficient. That helps p95 latency. There's some nuance with quantized models — we'll discuss with your workload.
04:03 Maya Thompson: Any gotchas on PHI with hosted?
04:07 Sofia Patel: We recommend private for PHI at scale, but hosted can be configured with limited retention and encrypted in transit and at rest; legal will want to check the DPA.
04:16 Daniel Park: Good. On billing — what's the trial credit and how does usage convert to committed pricing?
04:21 Marcus Liu: We'll include a pilot SOW with credits. If you convert to Dedicated, we can discuss reserved pools and committed discounts.
04:29 Maya Thompson: Perfect. One more technical: SSO audit logs — do you surface admin actions and API key usage?
04:36 Sofia Patel: Yes, audit logs include token-level usage, model calls, and admin events; retention is configurable depending on add-ons.
04:44 Priya Singh: For the pilot approval chain, we'll need a sign-off from Compliance and Infrastructure. Can Marcus coordinate the artifacts they need?
04:51 Marcus Liu: Yep, I'll create a checklist and share.
04:54 Daniel Park: Ok, wrapping up — who owns the weekly checkpoints?
04:58 Marcus Liu: I'll host weekly 30-mins, starting next Tuesday unless you prefer otherwise.
05:03 Sofia Patel: Recap I have: send onboarding guide + SSO/SAML doc + security exec summary (Sofia), schedule VPC deep dive (Rita), provide network contact and firewall rules (Daniel), set up weekly cadence (Marcus). Anything missing?
05:18 Maya Thompson: Please include expected data format for the anonymized EHR exports.
05:22 Rita Gomez: We'll add a sample payload and mapping table.
05:26 Daniel Park: Sounds good. Thanks all.
05:29 Sofia Patel: Thanks everyone, we’ll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
05:33 [meeting ends — 45 minutes total recorded as 00:45:12, some audio gaps noted during Rita's intro due to connectivity]
